name: Labels or Instructions
explanation: Any form control that asks for user input needs a label or instruction explaining what's expected. This includes text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, and dropdown menus. A label identifies what the control is for. Instructions can add detail, like a required date format or a password's minimum length. Neither needs to be excessive. A short, clear label is often all that's needed.
whoItAffects: People with cognitive, language, and learning disabilities depend on clear labels to understand what a form field is asking for. Guessing based on layout or placement alone is unreliable and error-prone. Screen reader users need a programmatically linked label to know what each field does. Visual placement near a field means nothing if it isn't connected in code. Anyone unfamiliar with a required format, like a date or phone number style, benefits from instructions that spell it out upfront instead of leaving it to trial and error.

codeExample.bad: Phone number
codeExample.good:
<!-- A label element is properly associated with the input via the for/id attributes -->
<label for="phone">Phone number (format: 555-555-5555)</label>
<input type="tel" id="phone">

howToTest: Check every form field on the page for a visible label or instruction describing what input is expected. Use a browser's accessibility inspector or a screen reader to confirm the label is programmatically linked to its field, not just placed nearby visually. If a field has no label, or the label exists but isn't connected in code, this fails.

check.question: A signup form has the word "Username" placed visually above a text input, but there's no `<label>` element or `aria-label` connecting the text to the input in code. Does this pass SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions?
choices: Yes, because a sighted user can see the label is meant for that field
No, because the label isn't programmatically associated with the input, so assistive technology can't determine it
Yes, because the word "Username" is self-explanatory
It depends only on the font size of the label text
